Northrop, Boeing, and LTV are significantly reducing the number of production labor hours required to assemble each successive B-2 aircraft, but are generally not meeting their goals for improving labor efficiency.
Assembly of the first two B-2 aircraft was completed in about 4.6 million production labor hours, exceeding the combined goal of about 3.3 million hours by 40%.

Based on current data, the production labor hours needed to assemble the third and fourth development aircraft could be about 3.6 million hours, or about 30% higher than the combined goal of 2.8 million hours.
The number of manufacturing defects has decreased on each successive aircraft, but was larger than anticipated, with defect rates affected by the discovery of incorrect fasteners being installed.
A total of 122,700 changes were made to engineering drawings through August 1990, including 29,500 in 1988 and over 22,000 in 1989 and 1990.
Estimates of work transferred to the final assembly plant have increased, with aircraft #3 seeing a 93% increase in planned transferred work hours compared to original estimates.
Northrop, Boeing, and LTV have made progress in establishing production management programs, but significant weaknesses remain in areas like work measurement, quality assurance, and tool proving.
